tip: Greek has no 'to' verb form – linked verbs chain with να (na): μπορούμε να δούμε (boroúme na doúme = we can that-we-see).
No 'a' when you just have something: έχουμε γάτα (échoume gáta = we have cat). Adding μία (mía) would stress exactly one.
Greek compares with 'from', not 'than': πιο φτηνό από το κέντρο (pio ftinó apó to kéntro = cheaper from the center).
Rooms and desks 'see' their view in Greek: βλέπει στο μπαλκόνι (vlépei sto balkóni = it looks onto the balcony).
Ongoing time takes the plain present: κάνουμε (kánoume = we take) cold showers δύο μέρες τώρα (dýo méres tóra = two days now) – no 'have been'.
Greek 'closes' electricity off: Κλείσε (kleíse = close!) τον γενικό διακόπτη (ton genikó diakópti = the main switch). Turning on is ανοίγω (anoígo) – open.
